newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Bank of Cyprus plans rights, debenture issues.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Cyprus plans rights, debenture issues.

text.p: The Bank of Cyprus said on Tuesday said it planned to raise a total of 75 million pounds ($162.7 million) with a 50 million pound convertible debenture issue and a 25 million pound rights issue.
Term of the rights issue will be decided at the start of 1997. The debenture will be issued at the end of the October. Terms have not yet been set.

Bank chairman Solon Triantafyllides told a news conference that between 35 million and 40 million pounds of debentures would be issued in Cyprus pounds abroad. The remaining 10 million pounds would be offered to local investors, with priorty given to existing shareholders.
Salomon Brothers would be lead managers and The Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation (CISCO) a member of the Bank of Cyprus group, would be an adviser to the bank for the issue.
"The debentures will be convertible into stock which foreign investors will be able to acquire," said Triantafyllides.
"It is the first time that stock of the group is issued abroad which represents between seven and nine percent of the share capital when converted," he said.
The proposed convertible bonds will be listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and will be the first Cypriot financial instrument to be listed on any bourse in Europe, he said.

Triantafyllides said the two issues, which would raise the bank's capital by 33 percent, would be used for "significant expansion" into Greece and other areas. Rights will be issued in May 1997. Terms will be announced at the beginning of next year, he said.
The bank also announced its half-yearly pre-tax profits rose 12.18 percent to 12.9 million Cyprus pounds compared to 11.5 million in the first half of 1995.

"These results are considered satisfactory, taking into account the problems that the Cyprus economy is facing, particularly the reduction in tourist arrivals that has negatively affected profits from foreign exchange income," said Triantafyllides.
